# @game-studio/settings

Collection of components to enable creation of settings menus for mobile, tablet and desktop

## Usage
#### Install
`npm i @game-studio/settings`

#### Import & Register Plugin
```js
import '@game-studio/settings/dist/main.css';
import SettingsPlugin from '@game-studio/settings';

Vue.use(SettingsPlugin, { deviceType: device.type.value });
```

The above will globally create all of the required Vue components ready for use. There are a number of Vue components for building settings menus which can be broken into 3 distinct "types":

- `settings-menu-xxxx` (used to build layout/structure)
- `settings-item-xxxx` (actual menu items)
- `input-xxxx` (low level input components e.g. checkbox)

In addition this package also exports `SettingsEventEmitter`. This event emitter allows us to fire events to show/hide/toggle the settings.

```js
import { SettingsEventEmitter } from '@game-studio/settings';

function onClick() {
	SettingsEventEmitter.emit('toggle/show/hide');
}
```

## `<settings-menu-xxx>` Components
These are the structural components used for building an overall layout for the settings menu. All settings menus must start with the `<settings-menu-root>` component as this provides top level styling/rules for the rest of your settings menu. The following structural components are available:

#### `<settings-menu-root>`
##### Description
The root of the settings menu. All other settings components must be contained within this component

##### Props
- **title** [string] (optional): The title of the menu. If this is used it will overwrite anything placed in the logo slot (see below)

##### Slots
- **default**: Where all other settings components should be placed
- **logo** (optional): Allows placement of a HTML to display a logo in the top right corner (only displays on mobile/tablet views)

##### Example Usage
```html
<!-- with a title -->
<settings-menu-root :title="menuTitle">
	<!-- other settings components -->
</settings-menu-root>

<!-- with a logo -->
<settings-menu-root>
	<div slot="logo" class="logo-styles"></div>
	<!-- other settings components -->
</settings-menu-root>
```

#### `<settings-menu-group>`
##### Description
This components will visually group settings together into a block of items. 

##### Slots
- **default**: Where settings components you want grouping should be placed

##### Example Usage
```html
<settings-menu-root>
	<settings-menu-group>
      <settings-item-info label="info 1" value="some info 1"></settings-item-info>
      <settings-item-info label="info 2" value="some info 2"></settings-item-info>
      <settings-item-info label="info 3" value="some info 3"></settings-item-info>
	</settings-menu-group>
    <settings-menu-group>
        <settings-item-info label="info 4" value="some info 4"></settings-item-info>
        <settings-item-info label="info 5" value="some info 5"></settings-item-info>
        <settings-item-info label="info 6" value="some info 6"></settings-item-info>
    </settings-menu-group>
</settings-menu-root>
```

#### `<settings-menu-accordion>`
##### Description
This component allows content to be hidden until the item is clicked. Once clicked it will expand to reveal its content.

##### Props
- **label** [string] (required): The label to display in the menu item

##### Slots
- **default**: The content that you want to show/hide

##### Example Usage
```html
<settings-menu-root>
	<settings-menu-group>
    	<settings-menu-accordion label="some setting name">
        	Your content goes here
       	</settings-menu-accordion>
  	</settings-menu-group>
</settings-menu-root>
```

#### `<settings-menu-sub-menu>`
##### Description
If you need a sub menu within settings then this is the component to use. A good example is "winners history".

##### Props
- **label** [string] (required): The label to display in the menu item
- **title** [string] (optional): The title of the menu. This will only display on desktop
- **wait-for** [function] (optional): A function that returns a promise. If this is provided as a prop, the menu item click will display a loading spinner and wait for the promise to resolve before showing the sub menu

##### Slots
- **logo**: Allows placement of a HTML to display a logo in the top right corner (only displays on mobile/tablet views)
- **default**: The content of the sub menu

##### Example Usage
```html
<!-- basic usage -->
<settings-menu-root>
	<settings-menu-group>
    	<settings-menu-sub-menu label="sub menu 1" title="sub menu 1">
            Sub Menu Content Goes Here
      	</settings-menu-sub-menu>
  	</settings-menu-group>
</settings-menu-root>

<!-- async content usage -->
<settings-menu-root>
	<settings-menu-group>
    	<settings-menu-sub-menu label="sub menu 1" title="sub menu 1" :wait-for="fakeLoading">
            Sub Menu Content Goes Here (will only display once "wait-for" has resolved
      	</settings-menu-sub-menu>
  	</settings-menu-group>
</settings-menu-root>
```


## `<settings-item-xxx>` Components
The following components are the "actual" menu items to toggle/change settings.

#### `<settings-item-info>`
##### Description
Displays a label and a value string, useful for displaying information such as version numbers.

##### Props
- **label** [string] (required): The label to display in the menu item
- **value** [string] (required): The value to show

##### Example Usage
```html
<settings-menu-root>
	<settings-menu-group>
    	<settings-item-info label="pulse" value="v1.0.0"></settings-item-info>
  	</settings-menu-group>
</settings-menu-root>
```

#### `<settings-item-action>`
##### Description
Displays a label and is interactive, allowing you to handle user clicks. Useful for things such as "my account"

##### Props
- **label** [string] (required): The label to display in the menu item
- **value** [string] (required): The value to show. For example, this could be used to show a game version number

##### Events
- **onClick** [function] (required): The function to be called when a user clicks

##### Example Usage
```html
<settings-menu-root>
	<settings-menu-group>
    	<settings-item-action label="my account" @onClick="onClick"></settings-item-action>
  	</settings-menu-group>
</settings-menu-root>
```
